evidence.quote: match Exports.dataVersion restored.Books with ... | Ok version when Some version <> text root "dataVersion" -> Error "The books in this file do not match its data version."
| Ready, Some books when not (books.Books.Customers.IsEmpty && books.Books.Drafts.IsEmpty && books.Books.Invoices.IsEmpty && books.Payments.IsEmpty) ->
{ model with Error = Some "Books on GitHub are moved with their repository, not with a transfer file."; Notice = None }, []

ARC-REV-01.rationale: All new domain rules are in Tier 2. Summa.Storage.Transfer decides the file's format, the checks on its books, the refusal order and the data-version match. Summa.Web.Engine decides the only-into-new-books rule, the GitHub refusal, the files-pack refusal and the import transition. The only Tier 3 change (AccountingWire) maps kernel event names to engine messages and decides nothing. app/index.html only binds the engine's view flag canTransferBooks.

evidence.quote: match Transfer.export manifest books ctx.Now with

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No effect is added below Tier 4. The time comes in as ctx.Now, which Transfer.export takes as a parameter. The download and the save are requested as data (OfferDownload, and SaveBooks through `save`) for the existing kernel or provider path to carry out. Transfer.read is pure and testable without effects. One caveat that does not affect this score: Transfer.fs, a Tier 2 module, uses System.IO.MemoryStream and System.Text.Json. These are in-memory serialization, not I/O, so they are not an effect under this criterion. They do break the instance's symbol rule ARC-SYM-01, though the requirement places the JSON file format in Summa.Storage.

evidence.quote: match Exports.dataVersion r, LocalSnapshot.encode manifest r with

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The change reuses the existing authorities for the facts it uses: Exports.Classification for the classification, Exports.dataVersion for the data version, LocalSnapshot.encode/decode for the snapshot and Diagnostics.describe for problems. The schema and version are single literals. The new books-hold-records predicate is defined in one place only. The reused 'This browser cannot offer downloads here.' text is a UI message, not a domain fact, and it matches the existing one.

evidence.quote: let contents (r: Receivables) = { Customers = r.Books.Customers.Count; Invoices = r.Books.Invoices.Count; Payments = r.Payments.Count }
| Ok _ when root.GetProperty("version").GetInt32() = Version && statedContents root <> Some(contents restored.Books) ->

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The contents count, which versions can be read, the contents-mismatch refusal and the preview text are all decided in Tier 2: Transfer in Summa.Storage, and the engine view in Summa.Web.Engine. The preview asks Transfer.read and Transfer.contents and does not re-check the file itself. No Tier 3 or Tier 4 code decides anything. app/index.html only binds booksTransferPreview.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No new effect. The preview is a pure projection over model text in the view, and the new contents check is pure. Change set 1's caveat still applies: Transfer.fs keeps using System.Text.Json, which is serialization rather than an effect.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The new contents fact has one definition, Transfer.contents, used by export, by the read check and by the preview. But the rule for an export's date (its UTC date as yyyy-MM-dd) is copied word for word from the import notice into the new preview instead of being shared. Version 1 is also written as a bare literal next to the Version constant. The copies agree, so this scores 1, not 0.
